column36: Scholarship Fair on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at Municipal Auditorium’s The Lex. This free event connects students with colleges, universities and scholarship opportunities in one convenient location, helping scholars take meaningful steps toward higher education and career readiness.

column1: Attendees will have the opportunity to meet with college representatives, explore admissions options and learn about scholarship opportunities. Some participating colleges and universities may grant admissions and award scholarships to eligible students on the spot. Students are encouraged to bring multiple copies of their unofficial high school transcripts, ACT/SAT scores and resumes.

Scholar Smarts KC is a Kansas City-based nonprofit dedicated to empowering middle and high school students through college access, academic preparation, career readiness and real-world learning opportunities.

The UMKC School of Medicine invites alumni, faculty, staff and guests to celebrate 55 years of medical education, achievement and community during its 55th Celebration and Reunion Weekend, taking place October 23–24, 2026. The milestone weekend will bring classmates and colleagues together for class-specific gatherings, graduate program celebrations, campus tours and opportunities to reconnect with the School of Medicine community.

column1:
The celebration culminates Saturday evening at the Kansas City Convention Center’s Kay Barnes Grand Ballroom with a reception, dinner and special program honoring the school’s history, accomplishments and lasting impact. Guests are invited to reconnect with former classmates, celebrate generations of graduates and look ahead to the School of Medicine’s continued growth and innovation.

EDspaces 2026 comes to Kansas City for a premier conference and expo focused on the future of learning environments. Bringing together education leaders, architects, designers, facilities professionals, dealers, manufacturers, and industry partners, EDspaces is where the people who design, plan, and equip learning spaces come together to explore solutions that support every learner.

column1: EDspaces is built around a powerful idea: learning environments shape outcomes. From classrooms to campuses, the event helps attendees better understand how physical spaces impact focus, teaching, collaboration, belonging, wellness, and overall institutional performance.

Throughout the event, attendees will have the opportunity to see real solutions in context, evaluate what is working, and explore what is next for education spaces. The 2026 schedule includes EDsessions, exhibit hall hours, plenary programming, networking events, and facility tours, with most functions taking place at the Kansas City Convention Center.
• Educational sessions focused on learning environments, design, planning, and facilities strategy
• Exhibit hall experiences showcasing products, services, and solutions for schools and campuses
• Networking opportunities with education, design, architecture, and industry professionals
• Special events including the Bold Women Collective Networking Event and EDfest
• Interactive discussions and tours exploring the future of education design and learner-centered spaces

Event: EDspaces 2026
Dates: October 28–30, 2026
Location: Kansas City Convention Center
City: Kansas City, Missouri
Designing for the Future of Learning

EDspaces offers a unique opportunity to connect insight with real-world application. Whether attendees are planning new facilities, improving existing spaces, or exploring innovative products and strategies, this event provides the tools, ideas, and partnerships needed to create learning environments where students, educators, and institutions can thrive.

Kansas City’s largest board gaming convention returns as Meeple-A-Thon takes over Bartle Hall for a full weekend of tabletop gaming, community, and charitable impact.

column1: Known as Kansas City’s premier convention for gamers and giving back, Meeple-A-Thon brings together thousands of players for an immersive experience spanning board games, card games, wargames, and tabletop role-playing games (TTRPGs).

Following its biggest year yet, Meeple-A-Thon 2026 is set to deliver an even larger and more dynamic event. Attendees can explore an expansive gaming floor, connect with fellow enthusiasts, and discover new games, strategies, and communities—all while supporting charitable initiatives.
Whether you’re a seasoned strategist, casual player, or new to the tabletop world, Meeple-A-Thon offers something for every level of experience.

column2: Organized Play: Hundreds of tables featuring board games, wargames, card games, and TTRPG sessions

column1: • Vendor Marketplace: Browse games, accessories, miniatures, and more from a wide range of exhibitors

column2: Programming: Discussions, workshops, and special events for players and creators

column1: • Community Atmosphere: Meet fellow gamers, join campaigns, and build lasting connections
• Charitable Impact: Participate in a convention dedicated to giving back through gaming
Roll the Dice in Kansas City

From epic campaigns to casual play, Meeple-A-Thon is where Kansas City’s gaming community comes together. Dust off your miniatures, gather your party, and get ready to roll—because this year, the adventure continues.

KC Pet Fest is Kansas City’s premier pet festival and pet expo, created for pets and the people who love them. We bring together local pet businesses, national pet brands, animal organizations, and thousands of pet lovers for one unforgettable, family-friendly event in Kansas City.

column1: More than a traditional pet expo, KC Pet Fest is an interactive festival experience designed to celebrate all pets — dogs, cats, reptiles, small animals, and more. Attendees can explore curated pet vendors, live demonstrations, educational sessions, adoption opportunities, entertainment, and hands-on activities built specifically for pet owners.

Founded in Kansas City, our mission is to create the Midwest’s most dynamic pet event that connects the local pet community, supports small businesses, and elevates the way our city celebrates our animals.

column1: This special ceremony recognizes the dedication, discipline and achievement of future firefighters who have committed themselves to public service, teamwork and emergency response. Family, friends, department leaders and community members are invited to celebrate this important milestone and support the cadets as they take the next step in their careers with KCFD.

The Kansas City Fire Department provides comprehensive all-hazards emergency services across Kansas City and is committed to protecting lives and property with ethics, compassion and professionalism. KCFD operates from 35 firehouses, including a station at Kansas City International Airport, and serves more than 510,000 residents across 319 square miles.

column3: Expo 2026 brings Kampgrounds of America franchise partners, team members, industry professionals, and outdoor-hospitality vendors from across North America to Kansas City for three days of education, collaboration, innovation, and community.

column1: Designed to help campground owners and operators strengthen their businesses and enhance the guest experience, the annual event features expert-led workshops, main-stage presentations, networking opportunities, social events, and an expansive expo showcasing the latest products, technologies, amenities, and services supporting campground operations.
• Educational workshops focused on campground operations, hospitality, marketing, revenue growth, and emerging industry trends
• Main-stage presentations featuring KOA leaders, industry experts, and keynote speakers
• An expo floor featuring vendors and innovative solutions for campground owners and operators
• Networking opportunities with KOA franchisees, team members, suppliers, and industry partners
• Special gatherings designed to welcome newcomers and strengthen connections across the KOA community

Kampgrounds of America, Inc. is the world’s largest system of open-to-the-public campgrounds, with more than 500 locations across the United States and Canada. Through its KOA Journey, KOA Holiday, and KOA Resort brands, the organization offers RV sites, tent camping, cabins, glamping accommodations, and amenities designed for a wide range of outdoor experiences.

Guided by a mission of connecting people to the outdoors and one another, KOA supports its franchise community through four core pillars: camper growth, revenue growth, operational excellence, and the strength of the KOA family.

column2:
Expo offers attendees an opportunity to exchange ideas, explore new solutions, celebrate shared successes, and build connections that support the continued growth of camping and outdoor hospitality across North America.

The North American Tour company stars in the first video look with Isaiah Bailey in the title role of ‘The Phantom of the Opera,’ Jordan Lee Gilbert as ‘Christine Daaé,’ and Daniel Lopez as ‘Raoul,’ Midori Marsh as ‘Carlotta Giudicelli,’ William Thomas Evans as ‘Monsieur Firmin,’ Carrington Vilmont as ‘Monsieur André,’ Lisa Vroman as ‘Madame Giry’ Christopher Bozeka as ‘Ubaldo Piangi,’ Melo Ludwig as ‘Meg Giry.’ Alexa Xioufaridou Moster plays the role of ‘Christine Daaé, at certain performances.’ In addition, the entire second year schedule of tour cities has been announced and includes Tempe, Las Vegas, Dallas, Nashville, Pittsburgh, Cleveland, Philadelphia and Boston. Mecum Auctions returns to the Kansas City Convention Center from December 3–5, 2026, for three exciting days of live auction action. Approximately 700 vehicles will cross the auction block, offering collectors, automotive enthusiasts and prospective buyers an opportunity to experience one of the country’s premier collector-car auction events.

column1: Guests can explore an impressive variety of vehicles, browse on-site exhibitors and experience the energy of live bidding in the heart of downtown Kansas City. Attendees interested in purchasing a vehicle may register to bid, while vehicle owners can apply to consign their automobiles for the auction.

Whether you are an established collector, searching for your next vehicle or simply appreciate automotive history, craftsmanship and performance, Mecum Kansas City delivers an unforgettable experience for car enthusiasts of all ages.

Soccer coaches, administrators, and referees of all levels are invited to unite with their soccer community for a truly unforgettable four-day convention experience in Kansas City, Missouri.

From expert-led lectures and live field coaching demonstrations to the newest gear and cutting-edge technology showcased in the Exhibit Hall, the United Soccer Coaches Convention is an essential event for anyone looking to elevate their soccer knowledge and strengthen their coaching résumé.

Coaching Education: Presented by world-class presenters, our collection of over 100 lecture sessions and field demonstrations will offer coaches at every level something to bring back to their own training sessions.

Building Connections: The United Soccer Coaches Convention features socials, meal functions, and award ceremonies that allow attendees to make lasting connections with other coaches and administrators.

The Business of Soccer: Featuring vendors from all corners of the soccer landscape, our expansive Exhibit Hall allows attendees to test out products and find solutions to assist with daily coaching and administrative duties.

Award Recognition: The association recognizes excellence in soccer, academics, and service to the game, through a multitude of awards events and installations.

column3: >Nobody’s Gonna Love You the Way I Do
column4: >, Ayana Evans brings her ongoing community engagement project C.R.E.A.M. (Cash Rules Everything Around Me) to St. Louis. Part block party and part opportunity fair, C.R.E.A.M. connects community members—such as students, job seekers, queer activists, artists, and people affected by the justice system—with free resources and supportive services.
column5: >Whether you, someone you love, or members of your community are looking for helpful paths forward, come to the C.R.E.A.M. Fair for a joyful communal space centered on care, creativity, and collective support.
column6: >Bright, comfortable clothes are encouraged—no suits allowed!

column3: >The C.R.E.A.M. Fair opens with the following offerings:

column4: >Engage in an interactive art activity with Freedom Arts &amp

column2: >• Discover the cultural resources of 4theVille, Show Me The World, and The Black Rep

column3: Reentry offers assistance on housing stability, financial security, emotional wellness, and community reengagement

column2: >Explore Mission: St. Louis’s Beyond Jobs program for individuals seeking meaningful employment, career advancement, and opportunities to build greater stability

>Sign up with St. Louis Public Library to get a library card and access to Tech Connect services, including website development, resume writing, and Creative Experience (recording rooms, 3D printers, laser cutters, digital creative software, and more!)
>Meet with admissions representatives from Harris-Stowe State University, Ranken Technical College, and Webster University
>Access health resources from the St. Louis City Health Department
>10:00–11:30 am / Play Date drop-in art activity

column3: >Performance by Harris Stowe State University Honeycombs and The Swarm Drumline

column2: >12:00–12:30 pm / Resume-writing and job-search workshop with St. Louis Public Library
>12:00–1:00 pm / Free headshots with Tyler Small

column3: >Panel Discussion with Chloe Bass and Hayveyah McGowan, moderated by Ayana Evans
>Step performance by Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity Inc.

column2: >Assemble a team of the best and brightest to have fun showing off your trivia knowledge!
>Hosted by the multi-talented Marina May Schleicher, a self-described STL hypegirl and co-host of the
column4: > podcast, our annual Trivia Night raises funds to support CAM’s free youth art education programs. Bring your own food and enjoy drinks from an open bar. In addition to a trivia contest, guests may compete in other party games like the infamous Booze Tower Ring Toss and Heads or Tails to win fabulous prizes. Bid on speciality items from local artists, makers, and restaurants in the silent auction.

column2: >8 Rounds of trivia featuring questions about pop culture, art, and more
>Bring your own food and enjoy an open bar
>Party games like Heads or Tails and the popular Booze Tower Ring Toss, where attendees can win their favorite libation

column1: • A silent auction with items from local artists, makers, and restaurants
Tickets are $500 for a table of 10 people and include an open bar. This is a 21+ event.

Sponsorships start at $1,250 with other additional options for in-kind support. Sponsors at the VIP level and above are provided with deluxe snacks. Presenting sponsors will receive table service. For information about sponsorship opportunities, email Director of Development Sherry Thomas or call 314.535.0770 x213.

column2: >Marina May Schleicher is a writer, curator, communications strategist, semi-professional talker, and self-described STL hype-girl. She co-founded Silver Space [rebranded to cool WIP], an independent editorial platform focused on contemporary art and culture, and co-hosts the cool WIP podcast, which features conversations with artists, curators, and cultural organizers. May Schleicher is the current Gallery Director of Opaque Collective where she organizes exhibitions, helps to develop public programming, and co-leads marketing and communications alongside the members. Left Bank Books and the Left Bank Books Foundation are delighted to present St. Louisan Sonny Buttar’
column4: s debut novel, The Daughters of Rosebud (2026).

column1: Join us at High Low Literary Arts Cafe to welcome Sonny Buttar for a presentation and book signing, free and open to the public. Sonny will be in conversation with St. Louis author and Board Chair of Kimbilio for Black Fiction, David Haynes.

The Daughters of Rosebud is a powerful exploration of sisterhood, family loyalty, and the courage it takes to heal. Teacher Salma Chaudhry lives a quiet life, avoiding all attachments. Growing up in small-town Rosebud, Salma and her older sister Asma were inseparable, but amid their mother’
column3: rigid expectations, Asma makes a choice that tears the family apart. The fallout changes everything&#8211
column4: and forces Salma to choose between her sister and her parents. Salma has spent years trying to forget. But as she recollects her past and considers reconciliation with her father, a young student opens a surprising connection to Asma&#8217
column5:
s past. In finally facing her history, Salma finds the bravery to love and hope again.

Travel from Estonia to the German Rhineland as conductor Kristiina Poska makes her SLSO debut in a concert that celebrates a variety of European folk music. Poska introduces us to the musical shapeshifting of a new composition by fellow Estonian, Ülo Krigul, and rising-star pianist Marie-Ange Nguci shines in Mozart’s sweet and playful Piano Concerto No. 21. Robert Schumann’s Third Symphony emphasizes the vibrant culture along the Rhine River in Germany, re-imagining folk dances, bucolic scenes, and the grandeur of a cathedral.

Manos PanAmerica is a Latin and North American fusion band that aims to reduce the gap between Latin and North America by playing its original and cover songs. It originated in 2023 in Saint Louis, Missouri, and is one of the few music projects in the city that incorporates various Latin genres and instruments into its performances. Some of the genres Manos PanAmerica covers include cachimbos, cumbia, bossa nova, joropos, boleros, huaynos, bailecitos, rancheras, corridos, and salsa. What starts as critiques on grammatical structure spirals into judgments on historical accuracy, erasure, professional ethics, and who ultimately is allowed to set the standard for Truth.

Grammy-winning jazz luminaries Branford Marsalis and Dianne Reeves come together to celebrate the timeless ballads of John Coltrane, which they have recorded and will release on the centennial of Coltrane’s birth this September. At the heart of the evening is the landmark 1963 recording by John Coltrane and Johnny Hartman—a masterwork of tenderness and restraint. Celebrate the enduring legacy of John Coltrane with some of the most intimate and emotionally transcendent music ever recorded in jazz.

column1:
In a near-future world massive flocks of birds have begun coordinated, lethal attacks on humanity. Two strangers, Nat and Diane, take refuge in an isolated, abandoned farmhouse in New England. Their fragile bond is disrupted by the arrival of a young woman, Julia, whose presence sparks deep-seated paranoia and suspicion. As the thin veneer of civilization starts to crack, are they as much a threat to each other as the birds themselves?

column1:
In a near-future world massive flocks of birds have begun coordinated, lethal attacks on humanity. Two strangers, Nat and Diane, take refuge in an isolated, abandoned farmhouse in New England. Their fragile bond is disrupted by the arrival of a young woman, Julia, whose presence sparks deep-seated paranoia and suspicion. As the thin veneer of civilization starts to crack, are they as much a threat to each other as the birds themselves?

column1:
In a near-future world massive flocks of birds have begun coordinated, lethal attacks on humanity. Two strangers, Nat and Diane, take refuge in an isolated, abandoned farmhouse in New England. Their fragile bond is disrupted by the arrival of a young woman, Julia, whose presence sparks deep-seated paranoia and suspicion. As the thin veneer of civilization starts to crack, are they as much a threat to each other as the birds themselves?

The sun’s warmth on your front porch. The burble of a nearby stream. The crackling energy of a summer storm. Feel the pull of nostalgia, wonder, and melancholy in works by George Walker, Samuel Barber, and Ludwig van Beethoven. Joined by soprano and St. Louis native Julia Bullock—winner of the 2024 Grammy Award for Best Classical Solo Vocal Album—the SLSO performs Barber’s poignant, brooding reverie on childhood alongside Beethoven’s sublime Pastoral Symphony.

The sun’s warmth on your front porch. The burble of a nearby stream. The crackling energy of a summer storm. Feel the pull of nostalgia, wonder, and melancholy in works by George Walker, Samuel Barber, and Ludwig van Beethoven. Joined by soprano and St. Louis native Julia Bullock—winner of the 2024 Grammy Award for Best Classical Solo Vocal Album—the SLSO performs Barber’s poignant, brooding reverie on childhood alongside Beethoven’s sublime Pastoral Symphony.
